claims.text: Sec. 1683 carries the note '50 USC 3373' and is titled 'ESTABLISHMENT OF OFFICE, ORGANIZATIONAL STRUCTURE, AND AUTHORITIES TO ADDRESS UNIDENTIFIED AERIAL PHENOMENA'. Sec. 1683(a) required the Secretary of Defense, in coordination with the DNI, within 180 days of enactment, to establish an office 'to carry out the duties of the Unidentified Aerial Phenomena Task Force, as in effect on the day before the date of enactment of this Act'.

Sec. 1683(c) requires the Secretary and DNI to designate 'one or more line organizations within the Department of Defense and the intelligence community that possess appropriate expertise, authorities, accesses, data, systems, platforms, and capabilities to rapidly respond to, and conduct field investigations of, incidents involving unidentified aerial phenomena' and to ensure those organizations have 'adequate personnel with the requisite expertise, equipment, transportation, and other resources necessary to respond rapidly'.

Sec. 1683(d)(1) directs designation of line organizations 'primarily responsible for scientific, technical, and operational analysis of data gathered by field investigations ... including with respect to the testing of materials, medical studies, and development of theoretical models'. Sec. 1683(d)(2) requires directives ensuring each such organization 'has authority to draw on the special expertise of persons outside the Federal Government with appropriate security clearances.'

Sec. 1683(f) requires a science plan to 'account for characteristics and performance of unidentified aerial phenomena that exceed the known state of the art in science or technology, including in the areas of propulsion, aerodynamic control, signatures, structures, materials, sensors, countermeasures, weapons, electronics, and power generation' and to 'provide the foundation for potential future investments to replicate any such advanced characteristics and performance.'

Sec. 1683(e)(2) requires an intelligence collection and analysis plan 'to gain as much knowledge as possible regarding the technical and operational characteristics, origins, and intentions of unidentified aerial phenomena'.

Sec. 1683(e)(1)(B) requires that DoD and IC military, civilian AND CONTRACTOR personnel 'have access to procedures by which the personnel shall report incidents or information, including adverse physiological effects, involving or associated with unidentified aerial phenomena directly to the Office'.

connections.edgeLabel: statutory basis for standing up AARO
connections.label: All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office (AARO)
connections.note: The Deputy Secretary of Defense approved amendments to the AOIMSG direction 'to meet the DoD requirements in section 1683 of the NDAA for FY 2022', establishing AARO 'to carry out the duties that were to be fulfilled by the AOIMSG'. The memorandum also renames the AOIMEXEC as the AARO Executive Council and makes AARO 'the authoritative office of the Unidentified Aerial Phenomena (UAP) and UAP-related activities for the DoD'.

sources.name: Deputy Secretary of Defense memorandum, 'Establishment of the All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office', 15 July 2022

connections.label: FY2022 NDAA Sec. 1683 (P.L. 117-81; 50 U.S.C. 3373)
connections.note: Section 1683 of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2022 (Public Law 117-81, enacted 27 December 2021) is titled 'Establishment of office, organizational structure, and authorities to address unidentified aerial phenomena', and sits in Title XVI, Subtitle E. It is the provision the board's section node is filed under.

connections.edgeLabel: office required to be established in coordination with the DNI
connections.label: Office of the Director of National Intelligence
connections.note: The FY2022 NDAA 'was enacted with a provision that requires the Secretary of Defense to establish an office, in coordination with the Director of National Intelligence (DNI), with responsibilities that include those that were to be assigned to the AOIMSG'; the Deputy Secretary acted 'following coordination with the DNI', and copied the memorandum to the Director of National Intelligence. The coordination requirement is statutory, not discretionary.

sources.name: Deputy Secretary of Defense memorandum, 'Establishment of the All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office', 15 July 2022

connections.label: Unidentified Aerial Phenomena Task Force (UAPTF)
connections.note: 'Consistent with section 1683 of the NDAA for FY 2022, I also direct the Secretary of the Navy to disestablish the Unidentified Aerial Phenomena Task Force (UAPTF) no later than the date the AARO is established, and to support the orderly transition of the UAPTF, including the transfer of any data, analysis, or other relevant material, to the AARO.' The statute did not abolish the task force directly; it required an office whose establishment the Deputy Secretary made the trigger for disestablishment.

sources.name: Deputy Secretary of Defense memorandum, 'Establishment of the All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office', 15 July 2022

desc: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2022, Public Law 117-81, approved 27 December 2021. Section 1683, codified at 50 U.S.C. 3373, is the first statute to require a standing DoD/ODNI office for unidentified aerial phenomena, superseding the Navy-led UAP Task Force. It mandates field-investigation line organizations, a science plan to explain performance 'that exceed the known state of the art in science or technology', and an intelligence collection and analysis plan on the 'origins and intentions' of UAP.
